ai_llms.summary: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton and USC ISI released FlashMap, a speculative-decoding drafter that proposes 16-token blocks in one pass. With Qwen3-8B it reached up to 6.14x lossless speedup on GSM8K, with lower, task-dependent gains elsewhere.
ai_llms.title: FlashMap drafts 16 tokens per pass for up to 6.14x lossless decoding speedup

ai_llms.summary: Anthropic's Haiku 5.5 starts at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens, about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5, and scores 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1. It is available on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, with effort controls and updated cyber safeguards.
ai_llms.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 priced from $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, scores 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1

ai_llms.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28 with access limited to selected cybersecurity organizations. It reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym and 71.0% on CWE-bench, and a lead on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 (59), with API pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens.
ai_llms.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber defense via Fairwind Program

ai_llms.summary: Meituan released LongCat-2.5 on November 2: 1.6T total and ~48B active parameters, 1M-token context, 128K max output. API pricing is $0.30 input / $1.20 output per million tokens.
ai_llms.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5: 1.6T-parameter MoE with 1M context at $0.30/$1.20

ai_llms.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to approved Daybreak Red customers, classified Critical under its Preparedness Framework. It scores 48.5% on ExploitGym and OpenAI's Linux pipeline produced 948 unique privilege-escalation exploits at about $359 each.
ai_llms.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber to vetted security teams, rated 'Critical'

ai_llms.summary: OpenAI and enzyme-design company Ligo released BioBasicsBench, 100 routine bench-science tasks covering data interpretation, error detection and recognising insufficient evidence. GPT-6 Astra scored 66.7%, GPT-6.1 Sol 62.0% and GPT-5.6 Sol 43.8%.
ai_llms.title: OpenAI and Ligo release BioBasicsBench; GPT-6 Astra tops wet-lab tasks at 66.7%

data_science_ml.summary: NVIDIA added Nemotron 3.5 Embed (8B, 1B and an NVFP4 1B), Rerank 8B and Parse 631M to its open Nemotron Retriever collection. The 8B BF16 embedding model scored 61.17 nDCG@10 on ViDoRe v3.1, first among dense retrievers.
data_science_ml.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 retrieval models; Embed 8B leads ViDoRe v3.1 dense retrieval

data_science_ml.summary: Mistral published the open weights of its multimodal MoE Large 4. Reported scores include 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and a 49.8% Coding Agent Index, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max.
data_science_ml.title: Mistral Large 4 weights released on Hugging Face with benchmark results

data_science_ml.summary: A benchmark of 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories. Across six agent configurations the best, Codex with GPT-5.5, completed 31.2% of tasks and passed 68.7% of individual tests.
data_science_ml.title: MLOps-Bench: best coding agent completes only 31.2% of real ML engineering tasks

data_science_ml.summary: llm-d v1.0, built by 500+ contributors across 25+ organizations in the CNCF Sandbox, adds multi-tenant flow control, zero-downtime DisaggregatedSet upgrades and session-aware KV-cache routing across vLLM, SGLang, GPUs and TPUs.
data_science_ml.title: llm-d 1.0 brings production-grade distributed inference to vLLM and SGLang

data_science_ml.summary: Snap introduced Alchemist, an agentic ML experimentation platform with a deterministic harness for plan validation, budget enforcement and human approval. In a Story ads feature-selection use case it cut cycle time from four weeks to two and removed 30% of features without metric regression.
data_science_ml.title: Snap's Alchemist halves ML experiment cycle time with a controlled agent harness

data_science_ml.summary: Google and Meta's PyTorch team introduced TorchTPU, a native C++ PrivateUse1 backend meant to replace PyTorch/XLA's lazy-tensor approach. It combines TorchDynamo compilation with a hybrid eager mode and was reportedly validated on 5,000 Hugging Face models.
data_science_ml.title: TorchTPU brings native PyTorch execution to Google TPUs

data_science_ml.summary: DiffuSpace released Clover-35B-A3B-Preview on October 30: a 35B total / 3B active-parameter diffusion language model with a selectable thinking mode under Apache licensing. It runs in SGLang and llama.cpp.
data_science_ml.title: DiffuSpace releases Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, an open MoE diffusion language model

data_science_ml.summary: Google's AI & Infrastructure team and Mercor released PLE, a benchmark of 29 public physical-engineering tasks with grading scripts, an evaluation container and an open leaderboard.
data_science_ml.title: Google and Mercor release Physical-Engineering's Last Exam for engineering agents

data_science_ml.summary: Google released XSE under Apache 2.0 as an export and inference runtime for OpenXLA. On short requests it delivered 2-5x the throughput of the best Python server Google built, with 30-70% less CPU time per prediction.
data_science_ml.title: Google open-sources XLA Serving Engine with 2-5x higher throughput

data_science_ml.summary: A benchmark of 56 physics research tasks from 42 physicists across 26 institutions found Claude Opus 5.5 leading with a 27.4% pass rate. The tasks cover the full research loop from literature review to manuscript writing.
data_science_ml.title: FrontierPhysics: no AI agent passes more than 46 of 168 research attempts

data_science_ml.summary: Thinking Machines Labs released Inkling 2 Small via its Tinker cloud service. In a company-reported test it doubled the forecasting score of a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B in 4.5 hours, and open weights are promised the following week.
data_science_ml.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small, which automates model fine-tuning

data_science_ml.summary: Decision Index v2 (Nov 8) rewards correctness plus calibrated confidence, raises private datasets from 25% to 45% and adds EvalSafe-O*NET-AA at 15%. Claude Haiku 5.5 Max scores 77 and GPT-6 Luna Max 76, ahead of specialist models Drex Max v1.1 and GLiDE v1.2 at 73.
data_science_ml.title: Artificial Analysis launches Decision Index v2, scoring calibrated confidence; Claude Haiku 5.5 Max leads at 77

explainers.summary: A cheap drafter proposes tokens and the target model verifies them in one parallel pass using rejection sampling, which preserves the target's output distribution exactly, so speedup depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted.
explainers.title: Why speculative decoding is lossless

explainers.summary: A stock is a claim on distant cash flows, so its value is highly sensitive to the discount rate, much like a long-duration bond.
explainers.title: Equity duration: why higher yields hit long-dated cash flows hardest

explainers.summary: Centrally issued stablecoins like USDT and USDC have issuer-controlled contract functions that can block specific addresses from transferring tokens, unlike decentralized assets such as bitcoin.
explainers.title: How a stablecoin issuer can freeze funds

explainers.summary: Prefill is compute-bound and decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, so serving stacks can split them onto separate GPU pools to improve utilization and latency.
explainers.title: Prefill/decode disaggregation in LLM serving

explainers.summary: In stress, forced selling to meet margin calls hits liquid assets regardless of fundamentals, so correlations rise and assets like gold and bitcoin fall alongside equities.
explainers.title: Why diversifiers sell off together in a crash

explainers.summary: Lazy-tensor backends like PyTorch/XLA record operations into a graph and compile it later, while eager mode runs each op immediately. This explains why TPU support has needed workarounds.
explainers.title: Lazy tensors vs. eager execution

explainers.summary: Masked diffusion LMs start from a fully masked sequence and unmask many tokens in parallel over several refinement steps, instead of generating left to right.
explainers.title: How diffusion language models generate text

explainers.summary: A multi-part offering splits one raise into maturities priced separately off the yield curve, and a new currency widens the investor base.
explainers.title: Why big issuers sell bonds in tranches and in several currencies

explainers.summary: The breakeven rate is the gap between nominal and inflation-linked Treasury yields, and it moves with oil because oil feeds near-term inflation expectations.
explainers.title: Breakeven inflation: how bonds price inflation expectations

explainers.summary: Exploit generation has an automatic pass/fail check, so models can generate many candidates and keep only the verified ones, which makes search and RL work well compared with fuzzier domains like physics research.
explainers.title: Why exploits are such a good target for AI: cheap verification

explainers.summary: Short-term rate futures price the expected average policy rate, so the gap between the implied rate and the current rate, divided by the hike size, gives a market-implied hike probability.
explainers.title: How hike probabilities are read from rate futures

explainers.summary: Repeating attempts averages out sampling noise within each task but not the noise from having only a small set of tasks, so small benchmarks still carry wide error bars.
explainers.title: Why five attempts per task doesn't fix a 100-task benchmark

explainers.summary: A CDS spread is roughly the annual default hazard rate times one minus the recovery rate, so it can be inverted into a market-implied default probability.
explainers.title: What a 1,000 bp CDS spread implies about default

explainers.summary: Core CPI strips out food and energy because they are volatile and mean-revert, so it is a better signal of persistent inflation, though energy can still leak into core and into expectations.
explainers.title: Why central banks watch core CPI, not headline

explainers.summary: The 2-year yield is roughly the average expected policy rate over two years plus a term premium, so it reprices fastest when the expected Fed path changes.
explainers.title: What the 2-year Treasury yield actually measures

quant_finance.summary: On Tuesday the Kospi rose 6%, the Philadelphia semiconductor index 3.6%, the Nasdaq 1.2% and the S&P 500 0.6%. Dell and Super Micro each gained about 7.5%, and WTI fell about 1.7% to below $100.
quant_finance.title: Kospi up 6% and Philadelphia semiconductor index up 3.6% as AI rally extends to US stocks

quant_finance.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand kept its official cash rate at 2.75% in a narrow vote that surprised markets. The New Zealand dollar fell more than 1% to $0.5583.
quant_finance.title: RBNZ unexpectedly holds at 2.75%, NZ dollar falls over 1%

quant_finance.summary: The FOMC held rates with Hammack and Cook dissenting; Chair Warsh said inflation is still too high. The 10-year yield rose over 4 bp to about 5.04% and derivatives price an 85% chance of a December hike.
quant_finance.title: Fed holds at 3.75%–4% on a 10–2 vote; December hike priced at 85%

quant_finance.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.8% after Microsoft and Alphabet results revived doubts about AI spending returns, even as SK Hynix reported roughly sevenfold profit growth and Oracle jumped 11%.
quant_finance.title: AI trade stalls after Microsoft and Alphabet results despite SK Hynix profit surge

quant_finance.summary: Hackers stole about $6.3B from Binance, which halted withdrawals and said it will cover customer losses. Circle and Tether froze about $2.38B of related assets, and bitcoin fell to a six-week low of $76,368.
quant_finance.title: Binance hit by record $6.3B theft; Circle and Tether freeze $2.38B

quant_finance.summary: Alphabet shares fell 12.6%, erasing about $500B of market value, after a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Amazon disclosed $42.4B of trailing-12-month cash burn, and Treasuries headed for their strongest monthly gain in almost three years.
quant_finance.title: Alphabet falls 12.6% on second straight negative free cash flow quarter

quant_finance.summary: Five-year Intel CDS widened by as much as 22.4 bp to a record 127.9 bp, Broadcom hit a record and AMD its highest since early 2019, after weak Intel and Amazon results revived AI-funding worries.
quant_finance.title: Intel's default insurance hits a record 127.9 bp as Broadcom and AMD CDS also surge

quant_finance.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 2.3% on weaker-than-expected Amazon and Intel results, bitcoin dropped almost 3% to about $76,600, and investors moved into Treasuries amid a global tech selloff.
quant_finance.title: Nasdaq 100 futures drop 2.3% after weak Amazon and Intel results

quant_finance.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% and briefly entered a correction, the S&P 500 dropped 1.8% below its 100-day moving average, and gold fell 3.3% and bitcoin 2.5%. The Nasdaq Composite lost 5.3% in October while the Dow gained 1.7%.
quant_finance.title: Nasdaq 100 drops 3.5% into a technical correction; gold and bitcoin fall with it

quant_finance.summary: French GDP fell 0.1% quarter over quarter in the third quarter as investment kept declining and exports weakened.
quant_finance.title: France's economy unexpectedly shrinks 0.1% in Q3

quant_finance.summary: Binance resumed service after the $6.3B theft, which the FBI attributed to North Korea. Customers withdrew $3.64B, 2.1% of its assets, and bitcoin and ether rebounded slightly.
quant_finance.title: Binance customers pull $3.64B after the $6.3B hack

quant_finance.summary: Brent fell to about $106 after Iran's supreme leader approved pursuing talks that could resolve the conflict. Stocks and bonds rose and tech led an S&P 500 rebound after its worst session since June.
quant_finance.title: Brent falls to about $106 as Iran approves talks

quant_finance.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates for the fifth time this year, taking them to an 18-year high, and signaled this could be the final hike of the cycle.
quant_finance.title: RBA raises rates a fifth time in 2026 to an 18-year high, signals it may be the last

quant_finance.summary: Democrats won both chambers in the November 3 midterms. Nasdaq futures fell as much as 1.5%, bitcoin dropped to about $75.7K, the dollar weakened across G10 and the 10-year yield fell 7 bp to 4.89%.
quant_finance.title: Democrats win Senate and House; Nasdaq futures fall, Treasuries rally

quant_finance.summary: Meta Platforms was reported to be raising $15B through a five-part US-dollar bond offering and issued euro-denominated bonds for the first time.
quant_finance.title: Meta raises $15B in five-part dollar bond and debuts in euros

quant_finance.summary: Brent fell nearly 9–10%, briefly below $100 and to about $93.50 in Asian trading, on expectations that a Democratic Congress would constrain Trump's Iran war response. Treasury yields fell to a two-month low and the dollar weakened to about $1.1273 per euro.
quant_finance.title: Brent plunges nearly 10% to about $93.50 as Treasury yields hit two-month low

quant_finance.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Wednesday, its best day in three months, and European shares hit a two-month high. Marvell fell 3.4%, Nvidia 0.8% and Intel 2% in premarket trading on data-center scrutiny under a Democratic Congress.
quant_finance.title: S&P 500 gains 1.6% while Nvidia, Marvell and Intel fall

quant_finance.summary: On November 5 the S&P 500 tech sector fell 7.3% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index more than 12%, both the largest one-day drops in over six years. The Nasdaq fell as much as 14% from its record and SoftBank's default-insurance cost hit a four-year high.
quant_finance.title: S&P 500 tech falls 7.3% and semiconductor index over 12%, erasing nearly $3T

quant_finance.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% as about $3.2T was erased, its deepest one-day drop since April 2025, then rebounded 1.4%. Taiwan stocks had their worst week since 2001 and tech bond spreads widened.
quant_finance.title: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% in its worst day since April 2025, then rebounded 1.4%

quant_finance.summary: Markets cut the implied chance of a December Fed hike from over 80% to roughly 70%, and of an ECB hike from 75% to about 60%, as growth fears from the tech rout outweighed the energy-driven inflation push.
quant_finance.title: December hike odds drop to about 70% for the Fed and 60% for the ECB

quant_finance.summary: Five-year credit-default-swap spreads on neocloud company CoreWeave rose above 1,000 bp, a record high and distressed territory, as investors reassessed the AI investment cycle.
quant_finance.title: CoreWeave five-year CDS tops 1,000 bp to a record

quant_finance.summary: Markets price about an 81% chance of a Fed hike on December 9, up from 71% a week earlier, after stronger-than-expected US employment data. The dollar index had its largest one-day gain in nearly six months on Friday.
quant_finance.title: Fed December hike odds rise to 81% after strong jobs data; dollar had biggest gain in six months

quant_finance.summary: Brent fell more than 2% to below $90 after Trump said he would hold off on new strikes on Iran, down 22% since end-October. The US two-year yield rose to about 4.56-4.58% and December Fed hike odds reached 84%.
quant_finance.title: Brent falls below $90 for the first time since August as Trump holds off on Iran strikes

quant_finance.summary: After hotter-than-expected US CPI, Fed Governor Waller said a 50 bp December hike should be considered if core monthly inflation again reaches 0.3% or more. Two-year yields rose by as much as 20 bp, the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and Nvidia fell 5.4%.
quant_finance.title: Hot US CPI: Waller floats a 50 bp December hike, 2-year yield jumps up to 20 bp

quant_finance.summary: Anthropic began marketing an IPO of almost $90B in new shares at an indicated valuation of about $1.4T. That is below the roughly $2T discussed in the market several months earlier.
quant_finance.title: Anthropic starts IPO roadshow at about $1.4T valuation, raising almost $90B

scandinavian_tech.summary: Swedish AI coding-tool company Lovable, with about 200 employees, is allowing staff to sell roughly SEK 800 million of shares in a secondary transaction rather than a new funding round.
scandinavian_tech.title: Lovable lets employees sell about SEK 800M of shares

scandinavian_tech.summary: Odense-based Velatir, co-founded in 2023 by a former Meta security executive, raised a €5M seed round led by existing investors Spintop Ventures and Ugly Duckling Ventures. It is building a real-time control layer for enterprise AI applications.
scandinavian_tech.title: Velatir raises €5M seed for enterprise AI control layer

scandinavian_tech.summary: Norwegian startup Jenz, building AI agents for retailers' back-office work, raised €540,000 pre-seed from Antler and Ada Ventures plus a NOK 1M Innovation Norway grant.
scandinavian_tech.title: Jenz raises €540,000 four months after winning a hackathon

scandinavian_tech.summary: Danish startup Cortas raised DKK 11M pre-seed from PSV Tech, JRNY Capital, EIFO and the founders of Flatpay and Spirii to build AI property-management software.
scandinavian_tech.title: Cortas raises DKK 11M pre-seed for AI property management

scandinavian_tech.summary: Oaiz, founded by people associated with the sale of cybersecurity company Debricked, raised more than SEK 20 million in its first round from Node, Icebreaker and Karaoke Club. It is building a platform to automate repetitive administrative work.
scandinavian_tech.title: Malmö's Oaiz raises over SEK 20M for administrative automation

scandinavian_tech.summary: Almi Invest CEO Joachim Karlsson says the state-backed investor is weighing a stop to its use of EU capital. A Riksrevisionen report argued that EU-capital rules have restricted its investments and weakened returns.
scandinavian_tech.title: Almi Invest considers dropping EU funding after audit criticism

scandinavian_tech.summary: Creandum raised SEK 7.5 billion for a new early-stage fund. Partner Fredrik Cassel, who led the Spotify and Lovable investments, expects about one in six portfolio companies to reach a $1B+ valuation.
scandinavian_tech.title: Creandum raises SEK 7.5B early-stage fund

scandinavian_tech.summary: Portuguese defence-drone company TEKEVER raised a €520M Series D at a reported €5.7B valuation, with €13M from Denmark's EIFO, and will set up its first operational Nordic presence in Denmark.
scandinavian_tech.title: TEKEVER raises €520M Series D and opens first Nordic base in Denmark

scandinavian_tech.summary: Danish company Claimlane raised a €5.6M Series A led by Verb Ventures to build AI agents that resolve after-sales issues such as returns, repairs and refunds, and to expand in the US.
scandinavian_tech.title: Copenhagen's Claimlane raises €5.6M Series A for AI after-sales agents

scandinavian_tech.summary: Stockholm-based Matters raised a $5M pre-seed round led by Swedish angel Jakob Johansson to build an AI-powered consumer bank.
scandinavian_tech.title: Stockholm's Matters emerges from stealth with $5M pre-seed for an AI-native consumer bank
